note: City of Waynesville campground on Route 66 on the bank of Roubidoux Creek, a trout stream, a short walk from Roubidoux Park's spray park, the Roubidoux Spring in Laughlin Park and downtown. Gravel back-ins (50 ft) and pull-throughs (58 ft). The city warns the creek can flood the campground in extended rains. --Claude
summary: City page and its reservation packet: $35/night ($175/week, $500/month) for back-in or pull-through gravel sites with 20/30/50A, water and sewer; heated showers/restrooms; reservations by phone or emailed application to City Hall. Waterfront lead: the creekside call is not supported - a ~20-25 m wooded bank separates the nearest pads from the ~10-20 m creek.
flags: WATERFRONT re-audit lead (stored creekside -> not waterfront): on Esri 0.4 m/px (leaf-off) the campground is one loop on the west bank of Roubidoux Creek at ~37.829,-92.2065. The nearest pads (the east row, outside the loop road) end ~20-25 m from the water, but that strip is a continuous wooded, brushy creek bank, not an open apron; the west row is ~60-70 m away behind the loop road. The creek there is ~10-20 m wide (creek, not river), and there is no creek-view value, so a screened creek resolves to not waterfront. For AWH: the city says guests may fish 'from the RV Park in the Roubidoux Creek', and in leaf-off imagery the bank trees are thin enough that a firsthand look could find paths to the water from the east row. The stored waterfront_evidence is only a commit reference.
Booking: reservable by phone - NOT first-come-first-served as the inclusion_evidence says. City Hall 573-774-6171 or the emailed application, paid before arrival; July-September near capacity.

Phone: the stored 573-528-8706 is the Park Superintendent's after-hours EMERGENCY number, and the city asks that it not be called for reservations ('Please do not call the Superintendent's number to make reservations'). Suggest phone -> 573-774-6171 (Waynesville City Hall, the reservation line).

Note corrections: the old note's 'a pool' is not on the city's pages (the nearby park has a spray park; swimming is in the Roubidoux Spring in Laughlin Park), and 'open year-round' is not stated either. The stored season (year_round, derived from that note) was left alone - the city gives no season; heated restrooms suggest year-round but do not say it.

Long-stay look: $175/week and $500/month are posted, and several east-row units in imagery have gear around them consistent with longer stays. Nightly stays are sold at a posted rate on a city page and the city requires every RV be roadworthy and removable in a flood. Local park; keep.

Flood caveat (written into the note): 'During periods of extended rains, the Roubidoux stream can and will flood the campground. Some of these floods have carried campers downstream.' Campers leaving an RV unattended must name someone within 30 minutes who can move it.
Pin: stored 37.8288,-92.2068 sits at the south end of the camping loop beside the office/lot (inside the campground; fine).
